title: finding(plugin-detail): `showReferenceRail`'s own docblock still teaches the ADR-0085-retired `detail.showReferenceRail` objectDef route — the third instance of the rot objectui#7998 corrected in the README, and the last live one
body:
Found by the `os-dev` lane delivering PR objectui#9811 (card objectui#7998) under that card's two-claims fence, and **re-verified by the reviewing seat** with the lane's own positive control re-run.

## What

`packages/plugin-detail/src/synth/buildDefaultPageSchema.ts` declares the live opt-in flag, and its docblock still teaches the **retired** objectDef route. Read on `origin/main`:

```
:154  /**
:155   * Opt in to the Reference Rail (aside region with
:156   * `record:reference_rail`). The rail is OFF by default — it fans out a
:157   * collection query per related list, which is wasteful on records the
:158   * author never intended to summarize. Set `showReferenceRail: true`
:159   * (per object via `detail.showReferenceRail`) to surface it; it then
:160   * emits only when `related` has at least 2 entries.
:161   */
:162  showReferenceRail?: boolean;
```

`:159`'s parenthetical is the defect. That route is an **ADR-0085 removed dead read**: this package's own CHANGELOG records the objectDef `detail.*` block — naming `showReferenceRail`, `hideReferenceRail` and `hideRelatedTab` explicitly — as *"no longer consulted"*.

## Measured, with a FIRING positive control

| probe | reading |
|---|---|
| ⭐ CONTROL — `options.showReferenceRail` in this same file | **hits** ⇒ the query fires and the live option is where the docblock's first sentence says |
| SUBJECT — any `detail.`-scoped rail key across `packages/`, excluding CHANGELOGs | the **only** hit is `:159`'s docblock line |

⇒ the docblock sentence is the last live teacher of a route nothing reads. The control is what makes the second row a reading rather than a dead grep.

## Why it is worth a card

⭐ **This is the third instance of one rot, and the first two are already handled.** objectui#7998 corrected two README claims about this same flag; PR objectui#9811 landed them. The route itself died under ADR-0085 and the README followed it down. This one survived because it lives in **source**, not in the document the docs card was scoped to.

The cost is the one that class always has: an author — **an AI author especially** — reading the declaration's own docblock writes `detail: { showReferenceRail: true }` into objectDef metadata, gets no rail, and has nothing to tell them why. ⚠️ And a docblock on a declaration is the most authoritative place a reader looks, which is why it outranks the README text that was just repaired.

## Why it was not repaired in the PR that found it

⛔ Deliberate, and the fence was the dispatching seat's: objectui#7998's order scoped the card to the README's two prose claims and said in as many words that if the taker found itself editing `buildDefaultPageSchema.ts`, it should stop and report. It did. ⭐ The alternative — a one-line drive-by into a source file from a documentation card — is how a scope-pinned diff turns into a review surface nobody priced.

## Shape of the remedy — ⛔ not decided here

Deleting the parenthetical is one line. ⚠️ What is **not** decided: whether the sentence should instead say the objectDef route was removed and name the surviving one, so a reader arriving from old metadata is redirected rather than merely un-taught. ⛔ Both are defensible and this card does not pick.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether any first-party schema, fixture or doc still authors `detail.showReferenceRail`. ⛔ Whether `hideReferenceRail`'s and `hideRelatedTab`'s own docblocks carry the same parenthetical — only the `showReferenceRail` declaration was read. ⛔ Whether the published `.d.ts` carries this docblock through to consumers; if it does, the cost is larger than an in-repo reader.

Refs: objectui#7998 / PR objectui#9811 (the two README claims, landed; this is the third instance) · ADR-0085 (the removed dead read) · `packages/plugin-detail/CHANGELOG.md` and `packages/app-shell/CHANGELOG.md` (the record of the retirement — ⛔ historical, not to be re-addressed).
